podcast.title: "Bridal Chorus" in "Ms. Jackson"
podcast.body: Outcast incorporated a recurring piano line from opera composer Richard Wagner's famed "Bridal Chorus," also known as "The Wedding March," into their hit song "Ms. Jackson." This was a clever touch, as the song's theme revolved around a man's refusal to settle down, contrasting with the traditional marriage anthem. "Outcast included a recurring piano line that they borrowed from opera composer Richard Wagner's famed bridal chorus, aka The Wedding March."

podcast.title: Comparison to Classical Music Dislike
podcast.body: Wagner serves as an example in a comparison used to critique the generalization of trap music. The speaker likens dismissing all trap due to a few artists to disliking classical music and consequently rejecting Wagner, emphasizing the need for a broader understanding. "eso es como si digo no me gusta mozar no me gusta bángler no me gusta la música clásica y el tercero que es más vergonzoso es lo que se llama la falacia narcisista."

srcs.episode: EL TRAP SÍ ES MÚSICA. (Aunque a lo mejor no te guste)

podcast.title: Use of Devil's Triad
podcast.body: Wagner, a highly influential classical composer, is noted for his use of the "devil's tri tone" (flattened fifth) in his works. His inclusion in this list highlights that this particular dissonant interval was a recognized compositional element within the classical tradition, long before its later controversial associations. "But then it did show up in a lot of classical compositions from people like Beethoven, Wagner, Debussy, Lyst, Sabelius, Bartok, dozens of others."
